data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"The preference for better-corroborated theories is indefensible on Popper's own terms and smuggles induction back in by implicitly asserting that past performance is a reliable guide to future reliability, reducing the methodology to psychological habit rather than logical rationality.","counterconditions":[{"case":"refuted if a coherent account can be provided where preferring a better-corroborated theory is justified solely as a method to maximize the severity of future tests without any assumption that the theory will actually succeed or remain unfalsified in the future","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"refuted if Popper explicitly distinguishes 'corroboration' as a report of past performance versus 'probability' as a prediction of future frequency in a way that validates action without inductive inference","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"refuted if the claim that Popper's framework reduces to mere psychological habit fails to demonstrate that no non-inductive logical rule can govern the preference","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"By advising scientists to prefer the better-corroborated theory for action, Popper implicitly relies on the inductive premise that survival of severe tests indicates future stability, creating a performative contradiction where the system collapses into crypto-induction whenever it leaves abstract methodology.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
